name: torc (torque)

attributes.attribute: ring of coiled metal worn about the neck
made of gold and richly decorated
appears on statues of gods and goddesses
found wearing torcs, possibly as human sacrifices

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The torc is a Celtic religious object. Archaeologists have found these rings of coiled metal across the ancient Celtic lands. Many torcs are made of gold and are richly decorated. They can be massive or slender. Sculptures and carvings show that people wore torcs about the neck, with the opening to the rear. The torcs appear on statues of gods and goddesses, so they may have marked divine stature. Humans may have worn them as a sign of religious dedication or high social rank. The bodies of Bog People are often found with torcs. This suggests that they may have been human sacrifices rather than criminals put to death.
